sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: NOT MEASURED — the clip confirms extracellular placement but reports no functional or trafficking assay result for the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: CATSPERε has a single TM domain (904–924) with one extracellular terminus: the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 20. The signal peptide (1–19) is cleaved co-translationally, so a tag placed after residue 19 emerges on the extracellular face. Python confirmed residue 19 = A and residue 20 = L. The paper explicitly states the HA tag follows the native signal peptide and is extracellular; because no residue number is named, the position is topology-derived from the single available extracellular terminus. The construct is described as truncated but is a membrane-anchored transgene (not a secreted ectodomain), so the surface-display inference holds. HA tag engineered at the N-terminus after the native signal peptide in a truncated CATSPERε transgene construct (Catspere-TG); the clip states the tag is positioned extracellularly. Signal peptide spans residues 1–19 (computed); insert_after_residue=19 is the unique extracellular terminus of this single-pass type I protein (extracellular 20–903, TM 904–924).

sources.claim: Sequences encoding the native signaling peptide and HA tag are placed at the 5′ region of the Catspere-TG sequences.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It supports a single terminal_n site at the mature N-terminus (after signal peptide cleavage at residue 19). The construct is described as 'truncated' (Catspere-TG), which introduces some uncertainty about whether it is fully equivalent to the wild-type full-length protein, hence medium confidence. No residue number is named in the clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived. No intracellular insertions or function-abrogating positions are reported in the ledger.
